title: Douglas v. Deutsche Bank National Trust Co., No. 24-CV-1099, Published Order

reading.body:
The headline of the reporting indicates a court in the District of Columbia faulted lawyers for a Deutsche Bank subsidiary over an AI hallucination. That places the failure at the point where generated text entered a court filing: a model asserted something false, and the false assertion was carried into a submission signed by counsel. The fault assigned by the court falls on the lawyers rather than on the model, which is where a filing-stage failure lands, because the signature on a filing is a human one.

Catching it would have required the lawyers to check the generated content against the underlying record before it was filed. The court's decision to fault them indicates that this check was theirs to perform and was not performed. Nothing in the available material shows whether the hallucination was a fabricated citation, a misstated fact, or something else, so the specific content of the false assertion is not established.

The summary supplied with this record is not a summary of the incident. It is a message from a system reporting that it could not read the encoded PDF it was given, which means the substance of the order, the nature of the hallucination, and any penalty imposed are not established here. A court faulting lawyers is a finding in that matter, and it does not by itself establish intent to mislead.
